title: Asset Management Strategy 2026-2031
author: P009
summary: Five-year strategy for Silvering's homes: safety and compliance first, full stock condition data, Decent Homes, EPC C by 2030 and a targeted investment programme led by Brenchley Gardens.

version_history.change: Stock data and EPC modelling added; Board workshop feedback

blocks.p: {{company.fictional_name}} owns and manages {{fact:homes_total}} homes across {{fact:schemes_count}} schemes. Most were built between the 1960s and the 1990s; a growing share are new homes from our development programme. This strategy sets out how we will keep every home safe, decent and affordable to heat over the five years to March 2031, and how we will pay for it.

table.sql: SELECT scheme_type AS "Scheme type", COUNT(*) AS Homes, ROUND(AVG(build_year), 0) AS "Average build year", SUM(epc_rating IN ('D', 'E', 'F')) AS "Below EPC C" FROM properties GROUP BY scheme_type ORDER BY Homes DESC
table.caption: Table 1 - Homes by scheme type

table.sql: SELECT epc_rating AS "EPC band", COUNT(*) AS Homes, ROUND(100.0 * COUNT(*) / (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM properties), 1) AS "% of stock" FROM properties GROUP BY epc_rating ORDER BY epc_rating
table.caption: Table 2 - Energy performance

blocks.p: Full compliance with the 'big six' (gas, electrical, fire, water, asbestos and lifts) is non-negotiable. Rosemount Tower, our only higher-risk building, has a building safety case and a resident engagement strategy under the Building Safety Act 2022. Damp and mould is treated as a safety issue under Awaab's Law.

We will survey 20% of homes each year, so that no home is more than five years from its last survey by March 2028. Today {{fact:ast_no_recent_survey}} homes have no survey within five years, including all new-build homes that have never been surveyed. Survey data will live in Keystone and feed the investment plan directly.

{{fact:non_decent_homes}} homes currently fail the Decent Homes Standard, all at Brenchley Gardens. We expect this number to rise as survey coverage improves, especially on older estates, and we will be honest about that with the Board and residents.

blocks.h2: Priority 4 - Warm homes: EPC C by 2030

blocks.p: {{fact:ast_epc_below_c}} homes are below EPC band C. Our target is that every home reaches band C by 31 December 2030. A fabric-first approach (loft and wall insulation, windows, ventilation) comes before low-carbon heating. Electric storage heaters at Rosemount Tower will be replaced with high heat retention heaters in 2027-28.

Planned investment is phased to protect interest cover. We will bid for Warm Homes: Social Housing Fund money for Brenchley Gardens and the 1960s-70s estates, and use our Coxheath Lane retrofit pilot to learn costs.

table.caption: Table 3 - Planned investment (approved business plan, March 2026)

bullets: Stock condition data incomplete or out of date (strategic risk SR10)
Net zero and EPC C by 2030 not affordable without grant (SR11)
Building safety failure (SR03)
Contractor capacity and cost inflation

blocks.p: The Director of Property owns the strategy. Progress is reported quarterly to the Executive Team and twice a year to the Board, with an annual refresh of the investment plan in the business plan cycle.

title: Compliance Assurance Report - Q2 2026/27
author: P023
summary: Quarterly assurance on the big six compliance areas for July-September 2026, updated with the Assure360 position at the end of October, including overdue EICRs, the Parkwood Court lift and Rosemount Tower fire actions.

version_history.change: Tables refreshed from Assure360 at 31 Oct for the Audit & Risk Committee

blocks.p: Gas compliance remains very strong. Electrical compliance has fallen below our 99% tolerance because a cluster of EICRs from the 2021 programme expired between May and October 2026 at the same time as we lost two electricians. Most overdue EICRs are no-access cases. A recovery plan is in place (see EICR Programme Recovery Plan).

table.caption: Table 2 - Unsatisfactory results and remedial works

blocks.p: The single overdue gas check is 8 Shepway Green, where Kentish Heating Services have made four access attempts. The case has been passed to Neighbourhoods for an injunction application. One home has an appliance capped as immediately dangerous with remedial work still outstanding; the resident has temporary heaters.

table.caption: Table 3 - Overdue EICRs

table.sql: SELECT scheme_name AS Scheme, check_type AS "Check", last_completed AS "Last done", next_due AS "Next due", open_actions AS "Open actions", overdue_actions AS "Overdue actions", status AS Status, assessor AS Assessor FROM building_safety WHERE status = 'Overdue' OR overdue_actions > 0 ORDER BY scheme_name
table.caption: Table 5 - Exceptions

bullets: **Parkwood Court lift (LOLER):** the thorough examination due 28 September was missed after Liftwise Engineering cancelled twice. It is now booked for 10 November. Liftwise is rated Red for repeated breakdowns at Rosemount Tower and Parkwood Court; Procurement is preparing a re-tender.
**Chatham Hill Court FRA:** expired 20 August. Fireguard Compliance carried out the new assessment on 30 October; the report is awaited, so the record still shows as overdue.
**Rosemount Tower:** see section 5.
**Legionella:** the AquaSafe contract expired on 30 September and is running on an extension letter until a new contract is let. This is a contract risk, not a compliance failure.

blocks.p: Rosemount Tower's fire risk assessment (March 2026, Moderate risk) has {{fact:ast_rosemount_fra_actions}} actions. The overdue ones are all about fire doors: six flat entrance doors that failed the self-closing and gap tests, and two cross-corridor doors on floors 9 and 11. The quarterly fire door inspection in October found {{fact:ast_rosemount_firedoor_actions}} items. The flat entrance door replacements were delayed by a 14-week lead time on certified doorsets and by residents refusing access. Doors are now on site and fitting starts on 16 November.

numbered: The Committee is asked to note **reasonable assurance** for gas, water, asbestos and lifts (except Parkwood Court) and **limited assurance** for electrical and fire safety.

title: Fire Risk Assessment - Rosemount Tower (March 2026)
doc_type_label: Fire Risk Assessment (Type 1 + flat entrance door sample)
author: P022
summary: Annual fire risk assessment of Rosemount Tower by Fireguard Compliance Ltd (12 March 2026): Moderate risk, stay-put strategy maintained, 11 actions including fire door replacements.

kv: 12-storey residential block, 1968, concrete frame, 88 flats, single protected stair, two lifts (one firefighting)
Type 1 (common parts, non-destructive) plus sample of 20 flat entrance doors (PAS 79-2)
Neil Ashworth, Fireguard Compliance Ltd (IFE Member, registered fire risk assessor)
Silvering Homes Ltd (Accountable Person under the Building Safety Act 2022)
Stay put (defend in place), supported by compartmentation
By 12 March 2027 or after significant change

blocks.p: The building generally provides a reasonable standard of fire safety for a stay-put strategy. The protected stair, dry riser, smoke ventilation (AOV) system and firefighting lift were all functional on the day. The main weaknesses are fire doors - both flat entrance doors and some communal cross-corridor doors - and a number of compartmentation breaches in service risers where cables have been added since the last survey. Housekeeping on floors 3 and 7 needs attention (mobility scooters and bicycles stored in lobbies).

rows: Six of 20 sampled doors failed: self-closers removed or not closing fully (4), excessive gaps at the head (2). Two had non-compliant letterboxes.
Doors on floors 9 and 11 do not close into frames; intumescent strips damaged.
Unsealed penetrations in risers on floors 4, 6 and 10 (new broadband cables).
Combustible storage in lobbies on floors 3 and 7; mobility scooter charging in lobby on floor 3.
Wayfinding (floor identification) signage meets the 2022 Regulations; 'Fire door keep shut' signs missing on 5 doors.
Premises information box contents not updated since 2024; no up-to-date list of residents who would need help to evacuate (PEEPs/PCFRAs).
Repair or replace self-closers on the four failed flat entrance doors and re-test
Replace six flat entrance doors that failed with certified FD30S doorsets
Repair cross-corridor doors on floors 9 and 11 (adjust, renew intumescent strips and seals)
Fire-stop service riser penetrations on floors 4, 6 and 10 using a third-party certified installer
Remove combustible storage from lobbies on floors 3 and 7 and write to residents
Stop mobility scooter charging in lobby; provide a safe charging store
Survey all 88 flat entrance doors (100%) to programme replacements
Replace missing 'Fire door keep shut' signs
Update the premises information box and share plans with Kent Fire and Rescue Service
Carry out person-centred fire risk assessments for residents who may need help to evacuate
Increase communal fire door checks to quarterly and flat entrance doors to annual (Fire Safety (England) Regulations 2022)

bullets: Dry riser tested (annual test September 2025, 6-monthly visual February 2026) - satisfactory
AOV system tested weekly by caretaker; annual service current
Emergency lighting monthly tests recorded; annual duration test current
Firefighting lift - satisfactory, but repeated breakdowns of the second lift noted (Liftwise Engineering)
Secure information box present at main entrance
Fire alarm: none in common parts (appropriate for stay put); smoke alarms in all flats tested at gas/electrical visits

blocks.p: This assessment reflects the conditions observed on the date of inspection. It should be reviewed if there is a significant change to the building, its use, or the people living there, or following a fire.

title: Resident Engagement Strategy - Rosemount Tower
author: P022
summary: How Silvering involves Rosemount Tower residents in building safety decisions, as required by section 91 of the Building Safety Act 2022.

version_history.change: Two-yearly review with residents; added door-knocking for fire door access and translated materials

blocks.p: Under section 91 of the Building Safety Act 2022 the Accountable Person for a higher-risk building must have a resident engagement strategy. It explains what safety information we share, how residents can take part in decisions about building safety, and how we will listen and respond. It applies to everyone aged 16 and over living in Rosemount Tower, including leaseholders.

bullets: The fire risk assessment summary and what we are doing about every action
The evacuation strategy (stay put) and what to do in a fire
How to look after your fire door, and why it must close by itself
Planned works that affect safety, and their dates
Results of checks on lifts, the dry riser and the smoke vents
How to raise a safety concern and how to complain

rows: Door-knocking and drop-ins on each floor
Twice a year, and before major works
Building safety team and housing officer
Consultation on safety decisions (e.g. door types, scooter store)
When a decision arises - at least 28 days
Translated materials (Polish, Romanian, Nepali, Urdu) and large print
On request and for all key notices

blocks.p: Your flat entrance door is a fire door that keeps fire and smoke out of the stair. We need access every year to check it and to fit replacement doors where needed. We will give at least 14 days' notice and offer evening and Saturday slots. If we cannot get access after three attempts, we may need to take legal action, because a faulty fire door puts your neighbours at risk.

You can report any safety concern by phone, MySilvering, email or to the caretaker. We will acknowledge within 1 working day and tell you what we will do within 5 working days. If you are not happy with our response, you can use our complaints procedure and then go to the Housing Ombudsman. You can also contact the Building Safety Regulator about a safety concern that we have not resolved.

subject: Rosemount Tower (HRB) - building assessment certificate: request for further information
summary: The Building Safety Regulator asks for more information on Rosemount Tower's fire door programme and resident engagement; Silvering's Building Safety Manager drafts and the Head of Assets reviews the reply.

messages.body:
Dear Ms Begum,

Building assessment certificate - Rosemount Tower, Maidstone ME16 8DU

Thank you for the safety case report and supporting documents submitted for the above higher-risk building. Having reviewed them, we need further information before we can make a decision.

1. The safety case report summary (v1.2) states that the six failed flat entrance doors identified in the March 2026 fire risk assessment would be replaced by 30 September 2026. Please confirm whether this work is complete. If not, please explain the reasons, the interim measures in place and a revised date.

2. Please provide the results of the 100% flat entrance door survey and your replacement programme.

3. Please provide evidence of how residents have been engaged on the fire door programme in line with your resident engagement strategy, including how you are dealing with refused access.

4. Please confirm the number of residents identified as needing help to evacuate and whether person-centred fire risk assessments are complete.

Please respond within 28 days, by 5 November 2026.

Yours sincerely,

Helen Okonjo
Case Officer, Building Safety Regulator

Priti,

Draft reply to the BSR below for your review - it's due on the 5th. Be aware the honest answer on question 1 is 'no'. The summary we sent said 30 September and the doors aren't in yet. Fitting starts 16 November. We still have four overdue fire door actions from the October inspection and three overdue on the FRA.

Draft points:

1. Not complete. Doorsets have a 14-week lead time from certified manufacturers and two residents have refused access. Interim measures: self-closers fixed on all four doors in April, weekly checks of floors 9-11 by the caretaker, letters to residents. Revised date 27 November.
2. Survey complete - 88 of 88, 19 doors need replacing in 2027 (attached).
3. Drop-in on floors 9-12 in September, letters, door-knocking. Two refusals now with Neighbourhoods.
4. 41 residents identified, 34 PCFRAs done, 7 outstanding (due 30 Nov).

I'd also like to update the safety case summary to v1.3 before we send so the dates match. I haven't done it yet.

Fatima

Thanks Fatima - this is the right approach. Be straight with them; they know the summary was optimistic.

Two changes please:
- On point 1, say who has signed off the interim measures (you, with Fireguard's advice) and attach Neil's letter.
- Update the safety case summary to v1.3 and send it with the response, so the BSR isn't working from the August version.

Gareth - copying you because this will come up at the residents' meeting on the 12th and at Audit & Risk. We may also need to consider whether any of this is reportable as a mandatory occurrence; my view is no, but Fatima please check with Fireguard.

Priti

Dear Ms Okonjo,

Rosemount Tower - response to your request for further information

Please find attached our response to the four points in your letter of 8 October, with supporting evidence (fire door survey results, replacement programme, resident engagement log, PCFRA tracker and our fire risk assessor's letter on interim measures).

In summary, the six flat entrance door replacements were not completed by 30 September as our safety case report summary stated. Fitting begins on 16 November with completion expected by 27 November. Interim measures have been in place since April. An updated safety case report summary will follow shortly.

Please let me know if you need anything further.

Kind regards,

Fatima Begum
Building Safety Manager

title: Building Safety Group
summary: Monthly Building Safety Group, 21 October 2026: Rosemount Tower fire doors and the BSR request, EICR backlog, Parkwood Court lift, Chatham Hill Court FRA and legionella contract.
agenda: Rosemount Tower: FRA actions, fire doors, BSR request

transcript.text: Morning everyone, thanks for joining. Neil, thanks for coming on from Fireguard. Can everyone hear me? Gareth, you're on mute I think.
Sorry - yes, here. Morning.
Okay. Actions from September first. Fatima, the big one was the six flat entrance doors at Rosemount by the end of September.

Yeah. So that's not done. The doorsets were ordered in June but the manufacturer quoted fourteen weeks, and they've only just confirmed delivery for the ninth of November. So we missed the thirty September date.
Which is the date we put in the safety case summary we sent to the BSR.
It is. And they've written to us - the letter came on the eighth - asking for exactly that. Is it done, and if not why not. We have until the fifth of November.
Right. We need to be completely straight with them. Neil, what's your view on the interim measures?

So the four doors with the closers were fixed in April, I re-checked those in the summer, they're fine. The two with the head gaps - they're the real problem, smoke would get past them. I'd want weekly checks on those floors, and I'd want the residents to know. I can put that in a letter for you.
That would really help. Thank you.
And the quarterly inspection last week?
Nine items open, four overdue. The cross-corridor doors on nine and eleven are still not closing properly. Those were meant to be done in April as well.
That's my lot, sorry. We had a carpenter on it, he adjusted them, and then they dropped again. Honestly I think the frames are the issue and it needs the specialist.
Okay, so let's put the cross-corridor doors with the certified installer and do them with the flat doors in November. Anil, can that go on the programme?
Yep, I'll add it as PW07, same installer, same visit.
And access?

Two residents have refused. One's on floor ten, one on eleven. Housing officer has been round. One of them is really worried about the door looking like a 'council door', I think we can sort that one with a choice of finish. The other one is harder.
I can take that one with Tom. We'll do a joint visit, and if we need to go down the legal route we'll start the paperwork, but I'd rather not.
Thanks Nadia. Okay, the full door survey.
Finished last week. Eighty-eight out of eighty-eight. Nineteen more need replacing, not urgently, so that's a 2027 programme.
Good. Right, domestic compliance. Rob.

Gas is fine, one overdue, 8 Shepway Green, four no-accesses, that's with Neighbourhoods for an injunction. EICR is the problem. Thirty overdue. Nearly all from the 2021 programme. And most are no-access - three or more attempts on about two dozen.
Thirty. That's going to look bad at Audit and Risk.
It will. I've got Brightline doing fifteen, but they're stretched, they're doing our repairs overflow too, and to be honest the quality on some recent jobs hasn't been great.
Yeah, we've got a contract meeting with them in November about the invoices.
I'm writing a recovery plan. Target: nothing more than three months overdue by Christmas, ninety-nine and a half by end of January.
Get that to me by the end of next week please. Jess, can you re-profile the programme so we don't get the same cliff edge in 2031?
Yes. If we spread it, it's about twenty-seven a month.
Lifts.

Parkwood Court LOLER was due the twenty-eighth of September. Liftwise cancelled twice. It's booked for the tenth of November. And they're still Red - Rosemount's second lift broke down three times in September.
We need to get that contract re-tendered. Can someone talk to Ben?
I'll do it.
Chatham Hill Court FRA?
That's on the thirtieth. Sorry it slipped - that's on us, we lost an assessor in the summer. Report about two weeks after.
And legionella - AquaSafe contract expired.
On an extension letter. Not a compliance gap but Ben needs to get the tender out.

Okay. Risk register - SR03, building safety failure. I think we keep the trend as rising. Anyone disagree? No. Right, AOB. The Rosemount residents' meeting is on the twelfth of November. Fatima, you're leading. I'll come. Gareth, will you?
Yes, I'll come. They'll want to hear it from a director.
Great. Thanks everyone, that's it.

recap.summary: The group confirmed that the six Rosemount Tower flat entrance door replacements missed their 30 September date, which was stated in the safety case summary sent to the BSR. It agreed interim measures, a revised November fitting plan including the cross-corridor doors, and an honest BSR response. EICR compliance is the main domestic concern with 30 overdue.
